items.title: Positive-gamma calm-up cluster across breadth, dealer positioning, and flow
items.note: Three independent surfaces line up bullish-but-contained: heatmap breadth is broad at 65.06% of 134 names, SPY dealers sit in positive gamma with the flip at 772.51 beneath the 777/780 wall band, and unusual options flow is call-heavy at 71% with the standout a same-day SPY 777 call. Positive dealer gamma plus broad breadth argues for a pinned, mean-reverting drift toward the 777-780 walls rather than a trend-day breakout, so strength chased into the call wall carries less edge than extremes reverting toward the 777.22 VWAP.
items.method: Cross-read the market-heatmap breadth metric, the options-structure and gamma dealer regime with its wall levels, and the options-flow lean, then reconcile them against the intraday VWAP to judge whether the up-tilt is a trend impulse or a gamma pin.

items.title: Equity risk-on drains real assets: metals and crypto lag while tech leads
items.note: Sector rotation is into XLK as XLE weakens, ETF momentum is led by tech (VGT 31.7%), and heatmap breadth is broad — yet the real-assets book is broadly weak, with silver (SLV) 10.2 in a downtrend, bitcoin (BTC-USD) 35.4 in a downtrend, gold (GLD) 33.4 mixed, and only industrial copper (CPER 50.2) near the top. The divergence reads as an equity and tech risk-on advance rather than a reflation or hard-asset hedge bid, so real-asset vehicles are a poor confirmation source and a weak diversifier this window.
items.method: Compare the sector rotation into/out tickers and the ETF-momentum leader against the real-assets model scores and trends, flagging the sign divergence between equity leadership and hard-asset momentum.

items.title: Singapore's global lead is local-equity-driven with a currency drag
items.note: Global rotation ranks EWS (Singapore) first at 85.2/100 versus ACWI, but the USD-leadership decomposition attributes the outperformance to local-equity strength offset by a small currency drag: over 63 sessions the approximate local relative return is +10.9% while the SGD translation subtracts about -0.4% and interaction another -0.07%, leaving USD-relative return +10.5%. The relationship reads as local-equity-led with an FX drag, so an unhedged USD holder captures slightly less than the local move and a firmer SGD would turn today's mild headwind into a tailwind.
items.method: Decompose the global-rotation leader's USD-relative return into local-equity, FX translation, and interaction components from the tool's decomposition summary, then interpret the sign of the FX drag for an unhedged USD holder.
